title: metrics.py: export_csv drops zero latency via truthiness
description:
## Problem

`Metrics.export_csv` writes summary latency with Python truthiness:

```python
writer.writerow([\"latency_min_us\", stats.min_us or \"\"])
writer.writerow([\"latency_max_us\", stats.max_us or \"\"])
writer.writerow([\"latency_mean_us\", f\"{stats.mean_us:.2f}\" if stats.mean_us else \"\"])
writer.writerow([\"latency_p50_us\", stats.p50_us or \"\"])
# p95 / p99 same
```

`0` and `0.0` are falsy, so a real zero (same-µs delivery, or a reservoir/min of 0 after the TX-start poll bugs) is exported as an empty cell, indistinguishable from \"no samples\". `None` (no data) and `0` (data) collapse. `test_csv_export_basic` uses latency 100; `test_csv_export_empty_metrics` has no latency rows to check.

Same pattern will blank p50 if the median sample is 0.

## Files

- `python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py` (`export_csv`)
- `python/tests/sim/test_metrics.py` (`test_csv_export_basic`)
close_reason: export_csv serializes latency with None-vs-0, so 0 us is written as 0 not an empty cell.
